question: According to recent reports, an unmanned surface vessel was detected in the maritime area of Lefkada, Greece. It appears to be a Ukrainian Magura V5 fitted with communication equipment, sensors and explosives. The competent authorities are investigating its route and the reason for its presence there12.

The incident raises serious questions about the ability to quickly identify small military or potentially dangerous unmanned systems in maritime zones of the Union, the presence of which may result in Member States becoming involved in wars going on elsewhere.

The EU has already developed tools to enhance maritime surveillance and information sharing, such as CISE, EUROSUR and the revised European Maritime Security Strategy, to improve situational awareness in the European maritime domain34. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What is its assessment of the incident in the light of surveillance and the need to identify small unmanned military systems?
Does it intend to strengthen CISE and EUROSUR so that they can respond more effectively to threats from USVs, unmanned vessels and hybrid maritime systems?
Will it consider establishing a European protocol for immediate notification and coordination in such cases?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.7.2026) Under the European Defence Fund (EDF) and the European Defence Industry Programme (EDIP), several calls were launched to enhance Member States’ maritime surveillance capabilities, including detection and neutralisation of unmanned threats.

EDF-funded projects on maritime domain awareness address such gaps by developing advanced sensors, AI-driven analytics and integrated C21 solutions. The Commission cooperates with Member States to strengthen the Common Information Sharing Environment (CISE), through the development of its classified network in 2026. This will enhance information exchange to address threats such as unmanned surface vessels.

CISE improves maritime domain awareness by enabling faster, cross-border coordination between Member States’ civil and military authorities. The Commission is looking into strengthening EUROSUR to better reflect threats at external borders, including hybrid threats and unmanned systems. EUROSUR focuses on situational awareness and information sharing.

Any strengthening would mainly concern better reporting, analysis, fusion services and the European situational picture, while national authorities are responsible for operational responses. The Action Plan on Cable Security provides for regional cable hubs to improve monitoring and threat detection near submarine cables, by aggregating relevant data and information.

These hubs should be supported by AI-based threat analysis to set a near real-time situational picture and allow faster response to incidents. The EU Action Plan on Drone and CounterDrone Security also addresses undersea and surface drones, building on the capabilities of regional cable hubs and launching pilot action to enhance maritime domain awareness.
